To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Schwannoma cells fail to align their cytoplasmic processes with neurons due to elevated Rac activity.
Schwannoma cells have a high level of Rac activity, and that the application of a Rac inhibitor to schwannoma cell lines restores Schwann cell-axonal interactions.

Schwann cell-axons interaction requires temporal regulation of Rac activity, and that the loss of temporal regulation of Rac is a key feature of schwannomas, which may be useful in future therapeutic approaches to schwannomas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how cells interact with each other.
the molecular mechanisms underlying axon-Schwann cell interactions and how these mechanisms are disrupted in schwannoma cells.
how Schwann cells and axons interact during development and in the mature nerve.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the temporal regulation of Rac activity is essential for Schwann cell-axonal interaction.
the temporal and spatial control of Rac activity is required for Schwann cell-axonal interaction, and schwannoma cell lines with NF2-mutants show abnormal temporal regulation of Rac activity.
Rac activity is necessary for Schwann cell-axonal interaction and is disrupted in schwannomas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the neurofibromatous type 2 gene is involved in suppressing Rac signaling.
Schwann cell axon interaction, which is disrupted in schwannomas is regulated by Rac.
the NF2 gene regulates Schwann cell morphology and that schwannomas have abnormal Schwann cell morphology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
schwannoma cells are unable to properly interact with axons.

we have identified a new role for the Rho GTPases, which are a family of proteins involved in regulating cell shape, in Schwann cell biology, and we have identified a novel therapeutic approach to treating schwannomas.
schwannomas, the most common tumor of the peripheral nervous system, have a defect in Rac signaling.
